title.roman: Tankhwah ki baat aur apne sawal

goal: Talk about salary politely and ask the interviewer two good questions.

phrases.text: I expect a fair salary for this role.

meaning.roman: Main is kaam ke liye munasib tankhwah ki umeed rakhta/rakhti hoon.

phrases.example: Based on my skills, I expect a fair salary for this role.

meaning.roman: Main baat-cheet ke liye tayyar hoon.

phrases.example: I am open to discussion if the role has good learning.

phrases.text: Could you tell me more about ...?

meaning.roman: Kya aap mujhe ... ke baare mein mazeed bata sakte hain?

phrases.example: Could you tell me more about the training?

phrases.text: What does a typical day look like in this role?

meaning.roman: Is kaam mein ek aam din kaisa hota hai?

phrases.example: I am curious: what does a typical day look like in this role?

task.roman: Mohazzab andaaz mein batayein ke aap munasib tankhwah chahte hain aur baat-cheet ke liye tayyar hain.

roleplay.model_answer: I expect a fair salary for this role. I am open to discussion.

roleplay.tutor_line: Our budget may be a little lower than that. What do you think?

task.roman: Agar company ka budget kam ho to mohazzab jawab dein.

roleplay.model_answer: I understand. I am open to discussion if the role has good learning and a chance to grow.

roleplay.tutor_line: Do you have any questions for me?

task.roman: Interviewer se training ke baare mein ek sawal poochein.

roleplay.model_answer: Yes, thank you. Could you tell me more about the training for new people?

roleplay.tutor_line: Of course. Do you have another question?

task.roman: Ek aur sawal poochein: kaam ka aam din kaisa hota hai.

roleplay.model_answer: Yes. What does a typical day look like in this role?

roleplay.tutor_line: Thank you for your questions. We will finish here.

task.roman: Shukriya ada karein aur khuda hafiz kahein.

roleplay.model_answer: Thank you very much for your time. I enjoyed our talk.

review_notes: The lesson teaches a polite, general answer and uses no salary numbers. Do you want a version where the learner says a range?
Turn 2 (a lower budget) is a common negotiation moment. Is the answer too soft for your market?
